record.title: China proposes protections governing platform work algorithms and consequential worker decisions
record.summary: On 8 October 2026, China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security published a draft cross-agency measure for public comment through 8 November. The proposal would require platforms to explain labor-management algorithms, prohibit specified forms of discrimination, and require human review before certain consequential decisions such as stopping task assignments or banning accounts, subject to a narrow emergency exception. The measure is a proposal, not adopted law; implementation and effects are not established.
organizations: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China
Ministry of Culture and Tourism of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security published a draft measure on workers in new forms of employment on 8 October 2026 and opened public comment through 8 November 2026, with six other agencies named as joint drafters.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The draft defines platform labor algorithms as decision rules and instructions used for automated scheduling, supervision, evaluation and incentives; Articles 27–29 propose worker-facing disclosure and explanation, restrictions on anomalous data in general assessments, anti-discrimination duties and human review before specified material decisions, with an emergency exception and subsequent review.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The proposal has been adopted, enforced, or caused changes in platform systems or worker outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The measure remains a draft under public consultation through 2026-11-08; the final text may differ.
No implementation, enforcement or worker-outcome evidence is established by the draft or status report.

brief.importance_rationale: If adopted and implemented as drafted, cross-agency rules for automated dispatch, evaluation and worker-impact decisions could materially constrain how large platform employers design algorithmic management and provide human review. The score concerns that possible deployment consequence, not confidence in adoption or measured effects.
limitations: This is a draft under public consultation, not a final rule or evidence of operative legal duties.
The draft applies to a defined class of workers using internet platforms under platform rules and instructions; it is not a general regulation of AI systems.
No platform implementation, enforcement action, or measured worker outcome was inspected.
organizations: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China
Ministry of Culture and Tourism of China

relationships.summary: Both are described in the MHRSS Nov 2 report, but this draft governs platform-worker rights and algorithms; the related development concerns expansion of an AI-assisted mediation/arbitration pilot.

technical.claimed_result: The proposal would establish minimum labor rights and algorithmic-management duties for covered platform work if adopted.
technical.demonstrated_result: The Chinese-language draft and public-comment process are published documents.
technical.mechanism: The draft treats platform rules as labor-management mechanisms, defines platform algorithms as automated scheduling, supervision, evaluation and incentive rules/instructions, and proposes disclosure, constraints on generalized metrics, anti-discrimination measures and human review for specified significant decisions.
technical.novelty: A cross-agency draft explicitly treats platform algorithms as labor rules and specifies disclosure, anti-discrimination and human-review provisions for certain worker-impact decisions.
technical.regime: Proposed Chinese national rules for labor performed through internet platforms under platform labor rules or instructions.
technical.reproducibility: Not an experimental result. The policy text is accessible in Chinese; adoption and effects remain unverified.
technical.strongest_baseline: The draft itself and the MHRSS-hosted Nov 2 status report confirm proposal/public-comment status; no independent legal interpretation or implementation evaluation was performed.

brief.title: China proposes protections governing platform work algorithms and consequential worker decisions
brief.why_it_matters: If adopted and implemented as drafted, the proposal would create explicit process constraints on automated task allocation, evaluation and worker-impact decisions for platform labor. It is relevant to deployment governance for algorithmic management, but does not establish rules for all AI systems or show that platforms have changed their systems.

related.summary: Both are described in the MHRSS Nov 2 report, but this draft governs platform-worker rights and algorithms; the related development concerns expansion of an AI-assisted mediation/arbitration pilot.

other.title: China says AI-assisted labor mediation and arbitration pilots now cover all provincial-level regions
other.summary: On 2 November 2026, China’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security reported expanding the “AI+ mediation and arbitration” pilot to all provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps. A May Shenzhen HRSS article says officials from 13 provincial-level jurisdictions shared experience at a workshop; it separately identifies Shenzhen as a designated pilot area in 2025 and does not establish that all 13 attendees were pilot sites or had deployed systems. The article, credited to Nanfang+ client, describes Shenzhen’s local system and reports usage and processing-time metrics that remain unaudited. The national expansion statement does not establish uniform operation, dispute outcomes, fairness, safety or independent effectiveness.
organizations: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China
Shenzhen Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
